searchResults.name: Big Four Ice Caves Trail
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington
searchResults.description:
This is a great, easy hike to absolutely stunning waterfalls on the upper cave. You may hear a lot of rumbling from ice falls or even witness the collapse of an ice bridge. Visiting the Ice Caves is definitely fun and it's a must-see in the summer time. 

Never go in or on top of the ice caves, as there is a risk of falling ice. Always proceed with caution and never go beyond your abilities and understand your limitations. It is recommended to bring water shoes and bug spray.

searchResults.name: Snoquera Falls
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington

searchResults.name: Myrtle Edwards Park to Elliott Bay Park
searchResults.description:
This is a pleasant, gentle, paved path with interesting views for the whole family - the waterfront, trains, boats, and a sculpture park nearby.

Accessibility: 

Equipment
This trail is likely accessible for visitors using wheelchairs, mobility equipment, or strollers.

Parking
There are 3 designated van-accessible spaces with striped access aisles in the paved parking lot off Alaskan Way West at the northwest end of the trail. 

Surface
The trail surface is paved asphalt and smooth and is...

searchResults.name: Granite Falls (Fish Ladder) Trail
searchResults.description: Along the river's bank, the Granite Falls (Fish Ladder) Trail features a fish ladder as a viewing platform. This vantage point lets you glimpse the Stillaguamish River meandering among boulders and rocks at low water. The ladder provides a great viewpoint, especially in the spring when the falls become a stunning stretch of churning whitewater, and the narrow section of the river creates tremendous flows.

searchResults.name: West Point Lighthouse via Discovery East Lot
searchResults.description:
This trail takes you from West Point Lighthouse to Discovery East Lot in Discovery Park. Discovery Park is a 534-acre natural area in Seattle's Magnolia neighbourhood. It overlooks Puget Sound and offers views of the Cascade and Olympic mountains.

The park features two miles of protected tidal beaches, a lighthouse, open meadows, dramatic sea cliffs, forest groves, active sand dunes, thickets, and streams. It's a great escape from city life, offering a sanctuary for wildlife and an outdoor...

searchResults.name: Talapus and Olallie Lakes via Talapus Lake Trail
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington
searchResults.description:
The Talapus Trail in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness takes you on a steady incline up to two lakes, Talapus and Olallie Lakes. The elevation gain is slow and steady and the hike feels very doable. Kids and dogs on leash will also have a fun time on this trail. There are a few bridge crossings and the trail can get a bit muddy in places, but it is very well maintained and easy to follow.

The Talapus Lake trailhead parking lot is at the end of Forest Road 9030. At about 1.5 miles in, just before...

searchResults.name: Sooke Potholes Riverside Trail
searchResults.location_label: Sooke Potholes Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description: Sooke Potholes Riverside Trail is a relatively easy route with little elevation gain. With various swimming holes, and a campground nearby this is a fun spot for a quick adventure. It's important to note that all-terrain strollers or motorized wheelchairs may be needed here for the unpaved surface. You may want to keep in mind there is no main 'viewpoint', as the main feature of the trail is getting access to different areas along the potholes for swimming and water activities.

searchResults.area_name: Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area
searchResults.name: Mount Si via Teneriffe Connector
searchResults.location_label: Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area, Washington
searchResults.description: The Teneriffe Connector Trail offers breathtaking vistas as it meanders through a lush, rolling forest. Ascending will take you to several noteworthy vantage locations. A section of the trail offers views of Rattlesnake Ledge and Mount Rainier. There's another overlook with panoramic views and a rest area indicated by an enormous stone bench. The trail eventually leads to a viewpoint from which you can get a good view of Mount Si. On clear days, the trail offers views of Whistler Mountain and...

searchResults.name: Sandcut Beach Falls
searchResults.location_label: Jordan River Regional Park Reserve, British Columbia
searchResults.description: While this is a short hike, it is very much worth the trip. You'll drop quickly through a lush portion of the forest and right onto a beautiful beach. Turn a left on the beach, and head down a short distance to the falls. There aren't any really technical sections, but there are some steps and some tree roots on the path. Depending on the time of season, the falls may or may not have a heavy flow.

searchResults.name: Sharpe Park Loop
searchResults.description: This trip covers the entire trail system in Sharpe Park, with a bit of backtracking.  The trails included are the Sharpe Park Trail, Wetland View Trail, Montgomery Duban Trail, Upper and Lower Loop Trail, Starbucks Connector Trail, Bluff Trail, Bluff Shortcut Trail, Cross Connector Trail, Sares Head Trail, and the Upper and Lower Trail. Some of the trails, especially the Bluff Trail, are a little challenging with the rise and fall in elevation and the ruggedness of the trail, but the payoff...

searchResults.area_name: West Tiger Mountain Natural Resource Conservation Area
searchResults.name: Tradition Plateau Loop
searchResults.location_label: West Tiger Mountain Natural Resource Conservation Area, Washington
searchResults.description: This loop starts near Issaquah High School and loops through the dense forest. The elevation gain is along the first half of the loop; you will enjoy a descent back to the trailhead along the second half of the hike. At one point, you will pass the remains of an old bus parked in the middle of the forest. There are a lot of trail crossings along this route, so downloading a map ahead of time is highly recommended to stay on the correct path.

searchResults.name: Mainline Trail
searchResults.description: This is a fantastic trail for mountain biking and hiking. There are lots of other little trail options in Paradise Valley Conservation Area that can be used to extend this route. It's a straightforward trail through nice undergrowth and minimal elevation change. The trails are well-marked and well-maintained but can be narrow in parts, so be mindful of cyclists. The trailhead is located on Northeast 205th Street.

searchResults.name: Mystic Beach
searchResults.location_label: Juan de Fuca Provincial Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description: This is the most direct way to get to Mystic Beach. While the Juan de Fuca trail starts (or ends) at the parking lot east of here, this trail is largely used by surfers and beachgoers for day trips and quick access to the beach. Folks have also reported that the trail is very rough with tree roots and that it can be very muddy but the beach at the end with the waterfall is worth it.

searchResults.area_name: Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area
searchResults.name: Teneriffe Talus Loop
searchResults.location_label: Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area, Washington
searchResults.description: Teneriffe Talus Loop takes you to Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area. The well-maintained trail leads through a shaded forest with creeks, bridges, and small waterfalls. Be prepared for steep parts and narrow sections. The viewpoint at the end offers great views of the surrounding mountains. Parking with restrooms is available at the trailhead.

searchResults.name: Wonderland Trail: Longmire to Cougar Rock Campground
searchResults.description: The Wonderland Trail leads hikers through Mount Rainier National Park to Cougar Rock Campground. The highlight of this route is the view of Mount Rainer and the gorgeous waterfalls. Expect a steady incline for the first half of the hike before descending via the same route. The trail can become muddy, and slippery, especially during winter when parts are covered with snow.

searchResults.name: Mount Ellinor Trail
searchResults.description:
Hiking up Mount Ellinor is an immensely popular route, offering sweeping views of the Olympic Mountains, Lake Cushman, and the Puget Sound. The trail is located in the Hood Canal Ranger District of the Olympic National Forest.

If you choose to summit Mount Ellinor, you have two trailheads to choose from. The mapped route on this page starts at the lower trailhead. This starting point is more gradual and does not require a Northwest Forest Pass. The upper trailhead is very steep, and requires...

searchResults.name: Beach, Fern Alley and Outbound Loop
searchResults.description:
Located between Seattle and Tacoma in the Puget Sound, this park is a fantastic destination for hiking, biking, kayaking, fishing and recreational beach activities. Beach explorers can find starfish, crabs, birds and raptors.

This 398-acre camping park features 3,301 feet of saltwater shoreline. The beach provides unobstructed views of the Puget Sound and opportunities for sea-life study.

searchResults.name: Kalaloch to Browns Point Trail
searchResults.description: The Kalaloch to Browns Point Trail offers a stunning beach walk along the rugged coastline, showcasing beautiful views of the vast ocean. Walking along the wide beach, you'll encounter driftwood and unique trees. This trail features a campsite on the beach, making it an ideal spot for those looking to immerse themselves in nature for a night. Along the way, you'll have the opportunity to observe diverse flora and fauna.

searchResults.name: Quinault Loop, Wright's Canyon, and Gatton Creek Loop
searchResults.description: This big loop takes you on a tour of the Quinalt area trails within the Olympic National Forest, offering a taste of each of the popular trails in the area. You'll begin at the Quinault Rain Forest Trailhead parking area, taking the Quinalt Loop to the Gatton Creek Trail. You'll cross footbridges through lush forest, eventually reaching South Shore Road. To complete this hike as a loop, you'll need to walk along South Shore Road for a short distance before hopping back on the trail. An...

searchResults.name: Deceiver Trail and Shy Bear Loop
searchResults.location_label: Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park, Washington
searchResults.description: This is a lovely scenic trail in Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park. The route winds through a gorgeous forest filled with interesting vegetation and wildlife. It begins from Jim Whittaker Wilderness Creek Trailhead, where parking is available. There is good elevation gain in the first couple of miles, with a lovely loop in the middle.

searchResults.name: Red Town Trail to Wildside Trail
searchResults.location_label: Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park, Washington
searchResults.description:
This is an awesome trail exploring the Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park. Along the way, there are mossy trees, streams, and a few bridges to cross. The trail is primarily flat, with some steps and inclines. The terrain is relatively easy, with a few rocks and exposed tree roots to navigate. 

Keep an eye on the map, as there are many intersecting trails in the park. You can easily extend your adventure by taking a detour to Steam Hoist to read about tharea's’s mining history. The trail...

searchResults.name: Jade Lake
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington

searchResults.name: Foothills Trail: Puyallup to South Prairie
searchResults.description:
This is a nice paved path behind the farms between Puyallup and Orting. It is good for cycling, hiking, walking, strollers, and kids.

Parking

There are two designated...

searchResults.name: Upper Goldstream Falls Trail
searchResults.description: The Goldstream Provincial Park is an area that has so much to offer from the highest trees to the impressive waterfalls to the diversity of the wildlife. The trail is following the stream to reach a majestic waterfall. During summer, it is possible to swim. It is recommended to bring water shoes or to be careful on the slippery rocks.

searchResults.name: Nature Trail, Cairn, and Sidekick Loop
searchResults.description: The Nature Trail, Cairn, and Sidekick Loop are well-maintained, but be prepared for some muddy spots, particularly after rain. The trail features a brief climb that quickly levels out. You’ll hike through a bright and lush second-growth forest. The terrain is shaded and rolling. Some sections of the trail are narrow. Keep an eye out for birds amidst the ferns and trees.

searchResults.name: Index Town Wall
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington

searchResults.name: Primitive Trail Loop
searchResults.description: This trail is located in the Dungeness Recreation Area in Sequim, Washington. The first leg of the loop is through flat terrain (not paved) in the forest, ending at the overlook for the Dungeness Spit. From here you can see great views of the spit, the functioning lighthouse, Mt. Baker, Canada, the Strait of Juan De Fuca, and many more mountains. If you head west you'll reach the trail for the spit. The remainder of the loop trail is paved and takes you right back to the parking lot. There is...

searchResults.name: Red Town and Wildside Trails
searchResults.location_label: Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park, Washington
searchResults.description:
This loop follows very well-cared-for trails throughout the forest. Many trees are covered with moss and the forest floor is covered in green ferns. You will cross Coal Creek at two points along the loop. This is a great option for kids and dogs!

The start point is at the Red Town Trailhead which is just off Newcastle Golf Club Road.

searchResults.name: Deception Pass Bridge and Beach Trail
searchResults.description:
Looking for a safe harbor and smooth waters? So was Captain James Vancouver in June of 1798. So he sent Ship's Master Joseph Whidbey with a crew in a small boat around the northeastern tip of what was later named Whidbey Island to search for the inner waterway to Port Gardener. Deceived as to the nature of this passage, he wrote on his chart "Deception Pass," and the name stuck.

Today the pass is a beautiful and exotic passage for all manner of watercraft as they make their way from the many...

searchResults.name: Piper's Creek and South Ridge Trail
searchResults.description: This loop takes you through Carkeek Park, a quiet retreat in nature within Seattle. The trail winds through the forest, featuring benches and beautiful water views on the western side. A bridge leads to a beach with a picnic area and great sunset views. Parking and restrooms are available at the trailhead.

searchResults.name: Kestner Homestead Trail
searchResults.description: Learn about homestead life on this flat, self-guided loop from the Quinault Rain Forest Ranger Station.

searchResults.name: Skyline Lake
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington

searchResults.name: Burke-Gilman Trail: Ballard Bridge to Bothell
searchResults.description:
The Burke-Gilman Trail runs more than 18 miles from Shilshole Bay in the City of Seattle to the City of Bothell where it intersects the Sammamish River Trail. It is a converted rail-trail along Lake Washington in Seattle. The trail is a paved, off-road facility over its entire length with the exception of an on-road segment in Ballard. 

Please use caution when using the bike path crossing under the Ballard Bridge as the train track intersects the trail at that point and there have been...

searchResults.name: South Beach and Hidden Valley Loop Trail
searchResults.description:
This trail takes you to Discovery Park on the outskirts of Seattle. The trail is well-maintained and easy to follow, offering amazing ocean views across the sound.

In late winter, you might spot the white blossoms of Indian plum along the trail. In spring, look for the bright yellow flowers of Oregon grape and the red blooms of wild currant. Parking is available at the trailhead.

searchResults.name: Seattle Waterfront Pathway
searchResults.description:
This pleasant paved waterfront walk weaves through restaurants, stores, and piers.

Accessibility: There are designated accessible spaces in the paved parking garages off of Alaskan Way at the southeastern end of the trail. All of them are van-accessible with striped access aisles. There are 2 designated accessible spaces in the paved parking lot off of West Marina Place at the northwest end of the trail. None of them are van-accessible with striped access aisles. 

The trail surface is paved...

searchResults.name: Creyke Point and Squeaky Point via Coast Trail
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail begins from the Aylard Farm Trailhead, which can be accessed by following Becher Bay Road just off of East Sooke Road. 

Light easy trail with nice ocean views and fresh ocean breeze with access to a sandy beach. Historic petroglyphs can be viewed at Alldridge Point. 

There are lots of roots and and rocks that make travel uneven but not difficult. Definitely a great walk for summer, take a quick dip or relax on the sandy beach afterwards.

searchResults.name: Iron Goat Trail
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington
searchResults.description:
Most of the trail is gentle, but there is a large set of steep switchbacks toward the beginning/end of the loop. The surface is gravel, natural, or paved bridge. There are stairs along this route. If you choose to go clockwise from this trailhead, you will go downhill and encounter the switchbacks at the very end of your hike. If you choose to go counter-clockwise, you will go uphill at the very beginning of your hike.

The U.S. Forest Service maintains this...

searchResults.name: Bogachiel River and Ira Springs Wetland Loop
searchResults.description: This scenic trail is picturesque, with lush ferns and evergreen trees covered in moss. Along the route, you'll navigate small bridges, boardwalks, staircases, and log crossings. Hikers can enjoy a scenic view of the river and occasional inclines. Depending on the season, the trail is also home to plenty of mushrooms. The journey begins from the Bogachiel Rain Forest River Trailhead, which has parking and restroom facilities.

searchResults.name: Kelly Butte
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington

searchResults.name: Nisqually Vista Trail
searchResults.description:
This family-friendly trail features beautiful views of Nisqually Glacier with a short walk to the Jackson Visitor Center. You may encounter snow through June and July. 

According to the park website, this trail is suitable for strollers but is not wheelchair-accessible due to a staircase at the trailhead.

searchResults.name: Trail of the Shadows
searchResults.description:
This loop heads around the Longmire Meadow Springs. Human and natural history come together in the forest and meadows of Longmire along the easy Trail of the Shadows. The trailhead is located across the main road from the National Park Inn in Longmire. Along its 0.7 mile-length, view bubbling mineral springs and explore a replica of an early homestead cabin. Discover the plants and animals that call this area their home, including deer, birds, and beavers.
